turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry about the wait, the queue's been hectic this morning. I'm Dr Naidoo. Your partner still outside?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, he's in the waiting room, I said I'd call him. Doctor, I'm really scared. I'm pregnant, and I've started spotting, and I've got these cramps.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, we'll go through it slowly. How many weeks are you, do you think?

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): That's the problem, I don't know. The last period was around Diwali, or after. I can't remember the day. So am I eight weeks, or ten? I've counted it three different ways.

[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): If it was around Diwali or just after, I'd put you roughly at eight to ten weeks, but I'm thinking aloud and I don't want to pretend that's exact. The scan will date it better than either of us. When did the spotting start?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday. So four days. Only when I wipe, brownish, and sometimes a bit pink. Is that a miscarriage? I'd rather you just say it.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): I can't say that from the story, and I won't guess to make it tidy. Is the bleeding heavy, soaking a pad, or is it spotting?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Just spotting. A panty liner does it. So that's better, hey? The baby can still be okay?
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Spotting can happen and the pregnancy carry on, ja. It can also be the first sign of trouble, so we check, we don't hope and leave it. How are the cramps?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Low down, like a period, comes and goes. Not the worst pain I've had. It's worse when I'm walking the corridors at school, and if I lie down it settles a bit.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any dizziness, fainting, pain at the tip of your shoulder?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. I haven't fainted. I am quite tired, and nauseous, but I'm managing.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): How long has the nausea been there?

[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Since I found out, about three weeks back. Two home tests, both positive. I actually did the second one twice, I didn't trust it. Sorry, I'm rambling, my mom's been phoning all morning and I haven't even told her.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ramble if you need to, we don't have to bring your mom into this. Have you vomited, or is it only nausea?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No vomiting. Just queasy, mostly mornings. I can still eat pap and everything. Is nausea a good sign, like the hormones are strong?
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Often it tags along with a healthy pregnancy, but it's not proof, so I won't hang the diagnosis on it. Burning when you pass urine? Any fever?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No burning, and no fever. I am weeing more, that's all. Is that an infection? Should I have antibiotics?
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Frequency by itself is common early on. No burning, no fever, I wouldn't reach for antibiotics today. Any medical problems, any surgery?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): My appendix came out when I was sixteen. Otherwise I've been well, hey. And I take folic acid, the five milligram one, every morning, since the test turned positive.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): By mouth, once a day. Good, you carry on with that. Any allergies, medicines or anything else?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing I know of.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Smoking? Alcohol?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): I've never smoked. There was one glass of wine at a braai, the weekend before I tested, and nothing after that. I feel sick about that glass. Did I do damage?
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): One glass before you knew is not damage I can point at. Let it go. What work are you doing?

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Grade two, a primary school here in Pietermaritzburg, and I've been on my feet all week. Did I cause the spotting, and must I stop work? Can I still walk, and is sex dangerous now? Also the sister said the sonar was broken yesterday, is it even working?

[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sonar was down yesterday morning and it's working today, I checked, so you won't be sent home unscanned. Work didn't cause this. Blood pressure is 118 over 74, pulse is 86, the tummy is soft, mildly tender just above the pubic bone, and there's no guarding.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Tender. That's bad, isn't it? Does that mean it's coming away? I knew I shouldn't have asked, but I have to.

[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mild tenderness goes with cramps, and on its own it does not mean the pregnancy is coming away. I'll look with the speculum. There's a small amount of old dark blood in the vagina, and the cervix is closed.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Closed means it's not a miscarriage right now, right? Why is the blood dark, not bright red? Can you see the baby with that?

[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dark blood has usually been there a little while, it's not a gush of fresh bleeding, and no, the speculum only shows the cervix, not the pregnancy. Putting it together, closed cervix, light spotting and cramps, I'm thinking this is most likely a threatened miscarriage. I also can't rule out an ectopic, that's outside the womb, not until we've scanned.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Ectopic, that's the one that can burst, hey? Am I going to collapse in the waiting room? Should you keep me in hospital? What are the actual chances?

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): You'd worry me more if you were faint, or bleeding heavily, or your pulse was racing. None of that is here, pressure and pulse are steady, so no admission this minute. I can't give you an honest percentage without the scan. Plan for today is a scan, and bloods.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Which bloods? Will there be a heartbeat? What if the screen is empty? How long do I sit downstairs? Can he come in now, I don't want the plan without him?

[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Beta-hCG, that's the pregnancy hormone, and your blood group, in case we need to know your rhesus status. The scan is transvaginal, an internal probe, uncomfortable for a minute but not really painful. Around eight to ten weeks we often see a heartbeat, though if the dates are earlier we might only see a sac, and that isn't automatically bad news. I'll fetch him.

[SEG0036] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Eish, sorry, I ducked out to shift the car and the robot took forever. Doc, she's been bad, the spotting's been about ten days. And she's been vomiting, she can't keep breakfast down.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Don't. The spotting started Thursday, that's four days, not ten. And I have not vomited once. I'm nauseous. That's the whole story. You weren't even in the room.

[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right, I'm hearing two versions. Somewhere between four days and about ten days for the spotting, and I'm not choosing a winner. Vomiting, you're not agreeing, so I'll park that. Nausea, she's been consistent.
[SEG0039] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ja, shame, maybe I mixed it with my sister's pregnancy. She does look pale, though. I worry.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm not pale, I'm scared. If today's scan is fine, is that the end of it? Do I come back? And if it gets worse tonight, do I wait for a date?

[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): Even with a decent scan today, let's see you in two weeks, to check the spotting has behaved and to talk it through properly. If it turns tonight you do not wait for that date.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): What is turns? A bit more pink on the paper? One clot? I'm going to inspect every wipe, I know I will.

[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): If you soak a pad in an hour, or the pain gets severe, or you feel faint, or shoulder pain starts, you go straight to casualty at the provincial hospital. Not a phone call first. Not in the morning. That's the strict part, and I need you to actually do it.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): And if it's daytime and I'm just worried, not soaking? Do I still go to casualty? What about school tomorrow, the children have a reading test. I feel guilty already.

[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): Daytime, if you're worried but not soaking through, phone the clinic and come back here, you don't have to sit in casualty for that. Work-wise I'd rest today and tomorrow, no whole day on your feet if the school can cover you. Pelvic rest too, no sex until the spotting stops.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): My evening walk? And folic acid, do I stay on five milligrams? Panado for the pain, is that allowed? I usually grab ibuprofen, is that the same?

[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): A gentle walk is fine, no jogging and nothing strenuous. Stay on the folic acid, five milligrams every morning, by mouth. For pain you can take two Panado, that's one gram, by mouth, up to four times a day when the cramps are sore. Leave the ibuprofen and the other anti-inflammatories while you're pregnant.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): And if the spotting just carries on, not heavier, just doesn't stop? I can't stare at a panty liner for two weeks and do nothing. Would you scan me again?

[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): If it does not settle, we might do another scan, rather than only waiting. We might, and I'm not booking it today. The scan today and the bloods today are the ones that are actually arranged. Let's see what those say before we stack more tests.
[SEG0050] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll bring her if it gets worse. She'll tell you she's fine when she's not, she's stubborn like that.

[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): I am not stubborn. I'm frightened of the words they'll use. Will somebody phone me the blood results, or is it only at two weeks? If they see a heartbeat, do these cramps even matter anymore?

[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll send the scan form through now, you go downstairs today, and the lab is on the way for the bloods. What we can interpret today, we will. The two-week visit is to pull the threads together, and if a result means sooner, the clinic phones you. A heartbeat would reassure me, it doesn't erase the cramps, but it makes a failing pregnancy less likely.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. I can do the scan if he comes with. Sorry I asked everything twice.
[SEG0054] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll come with. And I'll keep the phone on, doc.
[SEG0055] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. You've got the forms. Casualty if it turns heavy, otherwise I want to see you in two weeks.
[SEG0056] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks. And you'll be here, not a different doctor who doesn't know the story?
[SEG0057] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll book it with me. If I'm not on the day, the notes will spell out the plan, but the idea is you see me. Off you go, sonar first.
